2-door [[convertible]] | sp = uk }} The '''Bentley Continental GT''' is a [[grand touring car]] manufactured and marketed by the British company [[Bentley Motors]] since 2003. The Continental GT is offered as a two-door [[coupé]] or [[convertible]], with four seats. It was the first new Bentley released after the company's acquisition by [[Volkswagen AG]] in 1998, and the first Bentley to employ [[mass production]] manufacturing techniques. It was later joined by the [[Bentley Flying Spur (2005)|Bentley Continental Flying Spur]], a four-door [[saloon car]] variant. ==Origin== In 1994, [[Rolls-Royce Motors]] who at that time owned the Bentley brand, previewed a convertible concept car at the [[Geneva Motor Show#1994|Geneva Motor Show]] – the [[Bentley Java|Concept Java]]. The car was designed to be a smaller, more affordable Bentley, yet still exclusive in order to maintain the integrity of the brand.{{Cite web |last=Dean |first=Paul |date=2003-09-01 |title=Back Page: Java Jive |url=https://robbreport.com/motors/cars/back-page-java-jive-240298/ |access-date=2024-07-16 |website=Robb Report |language=en-US}} It was to appeal to a new range of potential buyers and generate increase sales volume for Rolls-Royce.{{Cite book |last=Hull |first=Graham |title=Inside the Rolls-Royce & Bentley Styling Department 1971 to 2001 |date=17 Feb 2014 |publisher=Veloce Publishing Lt |isbn=978-1-84584-601-5 |pages=118}} At the time the current [[Bentley Continental R]] was an ultra-exclusive £180,000 in the UK, within reach of a very select market, selling only 200–300 units a year. The Concept Java never went into production in the form seen in 1994, although 13 cars were made for the [[Sultan of Brunei]]. However, the Bentley Continental GT realised the concept of the Java as a more affordable Bentley, manufactured in much larger volumes.{{Cite web |last=Gold |first=Aaron |date=3 June 2019 |title=Bentley at 100: The History of a Proud British Marque |url=https://www.motortrend.com/news/the-history-of-bentley-100th-anniversary-feature/ |access-date=16 July 2024 |website=Motor Trend}} {{clear}} ==First generation (2003–2011)== {{Infobox automobile | name = First generation | image = Bentley Continental GT - Flickr - Alexandre Prévot (cropped).jpg | production = March 2003–2011 | assembly = | designer = Raul Pires, [[Dirk van Braeckel]] (2000){{cite web|url=http://www.drivingandlife.com/2011/11/delivering-dream.html|title=john-crawford: Delivering A Dream|author=John Crawford|work=drivingandlife.com|access-date=24 January 2015}} | platform = [[Volkswagen Group D platform#D1s|Volkswagen Group D1]] | related = [[Bentley Flying Spur (2005)|Bentley Flying Spur]]

{{convert|2485|kg|0|abbr=on}}: GTC | sp = uk }} ===Continental GT (2003–2011)=== [[File:Bentley Continental GT - Flickr - The Car Spy (11).jpg|thumb|left|Bentley Continental GT interior]] The vehicle debuted in 2002 at the [[Paris Motor Show#2002|Paris Motor Show]], followed by Le Mans,{{cite web |author=Newspress Ltd |url=http://www.bentleymedia.com/release/102/ |title=Bentley Continental GT to make dynamic debut at Le Mans |publisher=Bentleymedia.com |date=13 June 2003 |access-date=14 June 2016 |archive-date=14 May 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180514142021/https://www.bentleymedia.com/release/102/ |url-status=dead }} the 2003 [[Goodwood Festival of Speed]]{{cite web |author=Newspress Ltd |url=http://www.bentleymedia.com/release/86/ |title=Bentley Le Mans winners and new Continental GT in action at Goodwood |publisher=Bentleymedia.com |date=2 July 2003 |access-date=14 June 2016 |archive-date=1 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190301140144/https://www.bentleymedia.com/release/86/ |url-status=dead }} and the 2003 annual Bentley Drivers Club meeting at Silverstone.{{cite web |author=Newspress Ltd |url=http://www.bentleymedia.com/release/84/ |title=Bentley Speed 8 and Continental GT at BDC Silverstone |publisher=Bentleymedia.com |date=15 August 2003 |access-date=14 June 2016 |archive-date=1 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190301135952/https://www.bentleymedia.com/release/84/ |url-status=dead }} The car differed from the previous Continental R & T models in terms of its concept: although much of the car is hand assembled, it is a mass-produced car made in significantly larger numbers. It is not a coach-built car. The price at launch was less than half the price of the Continental R, giving the car a wider customer base. The Continental GT is equipped with a 6.0 litre [[twin-turbo]]charged [[Volkswagen Group W12 engine|W12 engine]], which produces a [[Deutsches Institut für Normung|DIN]]-rated power output of {{convert|560|PS|kW bhp|0|abbr=on}} at 6,100 rpm, and torque of {{convert|650|Nm|0|abbr=on}} at 1,600–6,100 rpm.{{cite web|title=Bentley Continental GT specification|url=http://www.bentleymotors.com/models/continental_series/continental_gt/specification/default.aspx|work=BentleyMotors.com|access-date=3 September 2009}} A [[Torsen]]-based permanent [[four-wheel drive]] is standard. It can accelerate from {{convert|0|to|100|km/h|abbr=on|1}} in 4.8 seconds, and go on to reach a top speed of {{convert|318|km/h|1|abbr=on}}. The Continental GT coupe features fixed front [[quarter glass]], but no [[B pillar]] between the front and rear side windows, a design which has been carried on through all subsequent generations of the car. Early models include a choice of 6 body colours (Diamond Black, Burnt Oak, Cypress, Neptune, Spruce, and Umbrian Red), 8 hide colours (Beluga, Burnt Oak, Laurel, Nautic, Portland, Saffron, Savannah, Saddle), 5 veneer types (Burr Oak, Burr Walnut, Dark Stained Walnut, Madrona, Piano Black) and 4 carpet and seatbelt colours (Beluga, Burnt Oak, Laurel, Nautic).{{cite web|author=Newspress Ltd ===2005 model year update, Mulliner Driving Specification (2004–2011)=== [[File:Bentley Continental GT Mulliner 000 since 2003 2006 frontright 2010-02-21 A.jpg|left|thumb|Bentley Continental GT Mulliner Driving Specification]] Changes to the Bentley Continental GT for 2005 include voice activation for the in-car telephone in six languages and increased interior trim options with the addition of magnolia hide, as well as carpets and seat belts that can be matched to either the main or secondary hide colour. The Mulliner Driving Specification includes 20-inch 2-piece 7-spoke alloy sports wheels with bespoke Yokohama Advan Sport 275/35 R20 tyres, drilled alloy sports foot pedals and footrest, a gear lever finished in knurled chrome and hide, two-tone leather and veneer combinations, diamond quilted hide to facings, doors and rear quarter panels; embroidered 'Bentley' marque emblem to seat facings, indented hide headlining and dark-stained burr walnut or piano black veneer. The vehicles went on sale in October 2004.{{cite web|url=http://www.auto123.com/en/car-reviews/new/2005-bentley-continental-gt-mulliner-driving-specification-overview?artid=33736|title=Car reviews from industry experts – Auto123|work=auto123.com|access-date=24 January 2015}}{{cite web|url=http://www.seriouswheels.com/cars/top-2005-Bentley-Continental-GT-Mulliner-Driving-Specification.htm|title=2005 Bentley Continental GT – Mulliner Driving Specification|work=seriouswheels.com|access-date=24 January 2015}}{{cite web|author=Newspress Ltd |url=http://bentleymedia.com/release/137/ |title=Bentley Mulliner creates Continental GT Coupé with added sporting edge |publisher=Bentleymedia.com |date=23 September 2004 |access-date=14 June 2016}} {{clear-left}} ===Continental GTC (2006–2011)=== [[File:Bentley Continental GTC 01.JPG|thumb|Bentley Continental GTC front view]] [[File:Bentley Continental GTC 02.JPG|thumb|Bentley Continental GTC rear view]] The [[convertible (car)|convertible]] version of the Continental GT, the '''Continental GTC''',{{cite web|title=Bentley Continental GTC introduction|url=http://www.bentleymotors.com/models/continental_series/continental_gtc/introduction/default.aspx|work=BentleyMotors.com|access-date=3 September 2009}} was first presented in September 2005, and was introduced to several world markets in the autumn of 2006. The roof is produced by [[Karmann]] in [[Osnabrück]], Germany. The GTC uses identical [[powertrain]] detail as the GT, and can accelerate from {{convert|0|to|100|km/h|abbr=on|1}} in 5.1 seconds.{{cite web|title=Bentley Continental GTC specification|url=http://www.bentleymotors.com/models/continental_series/continental_gtc/specification/default.aspx|work=BentleyMotors.com|access-date=3 September 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090829232932/http://www.bentleymotors.com/models/continental_series/continental_gtc/specification/default.aspx|archive-date=29 August 2009}} With the roof up, it can reach a top speed of {{convert|314|km/h|1|abbr=on}}, though with the roof down top speed drops to {{convert|305|km/h|1|abbr=on}}. The vehicle was unveiled at the [[New York International Auto Show#2006|2006 New York International Auto Show]],{{cite web |author=Newspress Ltd |url=http://bentleymedia.com/release/200/ |title=Bentley Continental GTC – Media information |publisher=Bentleymedia.com |date=12 April 2006 |access-date=14 June 2016 |archive-date=19 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151119122740/http://bentleymedia.com/release/200/ |url-status=dead }} followed by the C. de Salamanca in Seville.{{cite web|author=Newspress Ltd |url=http://bentleymedia.com/release/131/ |title=Bentley Marbella And José Carlos De Salamanca Host An Exclusive Reception in Seville |publisher=Bentleymedia.com |date=19 May 2008 |access-date=14 June 2016}} The vehicle went on sale in late 2006.{{cite web|author=Newspress Ltd |url=http://bentleymedia.com/release/215/ |title=Bentley announces stunning new convertible version of the Continental GT |publisher=Bentleymedia.com |date=26 September 2005 |access-date=14 June 2016}}{{clear}} ===2008 model year update, Continental GT Speed, Mulliner Driving Specification (2007–2011)=== [[File:2007-2010 Bentley Continental (3W) GT Speed coupe (2010-05-22) 01.jpg|thumb|Bentley Continental GT Speed front view]] [[File:2007-2010 Bentley Continental (3W) GT Speed coupe (2010-05-22) 02.jpg|thumb|Bentley Continental GT Speed rear view]] Changes to the Continental GT for 2008 include a {{convert|35|kg|lb|0|abbr=on}} reduction in kerb weight due primarily to optimisation of suspension and cooling system components and an increased use of aluminium parts in the suspension. Other changes include a revised Servotronic [[power steering]] for improved feel and feedback, optional fade-resistant carbon ceramic brakes provide improved brake feel (only available on 20-inch wheels), new, more upright front grille and larger lower air intakes give improved airflow to aid engine cooling; chromed headlamp bezels, two new exterior paint colours (Cumbrian Green and Granite), two new leather hide colours (Newmarket Tan and Cumbrian Green), new low-friction dampers, new 'Sport Traction' mode for the Bosch 8.1 ESP system and a Bentley 'B' brake pedal. The Mulliner Driving Specification includes drilled alloy sport foot-pedals, knurled chrome/hide gear lever, diamond quilted hide to seat facings, doors and rear quarter panels. The Continental GT Speed is a version of the Continental GT with increased engine power to {{convert|608|PS|kW bhp|0|abbr=on}} and {{convert|750|Nm|lbft|0|abbr=on}} of torque. It also includes a lowered [[ride height]], uprated spring/damper settings and uprated anti-roll bars for improved agility and body control; unique 9.5Jx20-inch wheels with bespoke [[Pirelli]] P-Zero performance tyres, retuned speed-sensitive Servotronic system, solid-mounted front subframe and stiffer rear bushings; 'Dynamic' mode for the Bosch 8.1 ESP system, front grille and lower air intakes in dark-tinted chrome matrix and wider rifled sports exhaust tail pipes. The Continental GT Speed was unveiled at Laguna Village Polo in 2007,{{cite web |author=Newspress Ltd |date=17 September 2007 |title=Bentley Marbella presents the new Bentley Continental GT Speed |url=http://www.bentleymedia.com/release/173/ |access-date=14 June 2016 |publisher=Bentleymedia.com}} followed by the [[Frankfurt Motor Show#2007|2007 Frankfurt Motor Show]].{{cite web |author=John 2015 |work=Autoblog|date=3 August 2007 }} {{clear}} ===2009 Continental GTC update, Continental GTC Speed, Mulliner Driving Specification (2009–2011)=== [[File:Bentley Continental GTC Speed 20090720 front-1.JPG|thumb|right|2009 Bentley Continental GTC Speed front view]] [[File:Bentley Continental GTC Speed 20090720 rear.JPG|thumb|right|2009 Bentley Continental GTC Speed rear view]] Changes to the Continental GTC for 2009 include a new more upright front grille, larger lower air intake, chrome headlamp bezels, retuned Servotronic power steering for improved feedback and feel, new optional [[Follow-to-stop]], [[radar]]–based [[Adaptive Cruise Control]], optional carbon ceramic brakes with 420 mm front and 356 mm rear discs and eight-piston callipers (only available with 20 – inch wheels), two new exterior colours (Aquamarine, Blue Crystal) and a new interior colour (Aquamarine). The Mulliner Driving Specification includes a choice of three standard veneers (Burr Walnut, Dark Stained Burr Walnut, Piano Black, drilled alloy sport foot-pedals, gear lever finished in knurled chrome and hide, diamond quilted hide to seat facings, doors and rear quarter panels; embroidered Bentley emblem to seat facings, 20-inch two-piece alloy sports wheels (GTC only) or 20-inch multi-spoke alloy wheels in Dark Tint painted finish (GTC Speed only). The Continental GTC Speed is based on the Continental GTC with Mulliner Driving Specification. It is equipped with the engine from the Continental GT Speed as well as radiator and lower air intake grilles with a dark tinted matrix, 9.5Jx20-inch multi-spoke alloy wheels, Bentley-bespoke [[Pirelli]] PZero tyres, lowered suspension by 10 mm at the front and 15 mm, wider twin-rifled exhaust tail pipes and a new boot-mounted lip spoiler. The vehicle was unveiled at the [[North American International Auto Show#2009|2009 North American International Auto Show]].{{cite web|url=http://www.autoblog.com/2009/01/11/detroit-2009-bentley-continental-gtc-speed-brings-beauty-with-a/|title=Detroit 2009: Bentley Continental GTC Speed brings beauty with a quickness|author=Chris Paukert|work=Autoblog|date=11 January 2009 |access-date=24 January 2015}}{{cite web |author=Newspress Ltd |url=http://bentleymedia.com/release/62/ |title=The new GTC Speed builds on the success of Continental GTC |publisher=Bentleymedia.com |date=6 January 2009 |access-date=14 June 2016 |archive-date=1 April 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150401042022/http://bentleymedia.com/release/62/ |url-status=dead }} {{clear}} ===Continental GT Series 51 (2009)=== [[File:Mondial de l'Automobile 2010, Paris - France (5058163703).jpg|thumb|Bentley Continental GT Series 51 (France)]] The Series 51 models include additional vehicle customisation options for the Continental GT and GTC, such as use of non-indented hide for diamond quilting and contrast piping for the seats and doors as well as bespoke Series 51 treadplates. Other options include Dark and Bright 'Engine Spin' aluminium dashboard and centre console options, Amboyna veneer, colour matched overmats and boot carpets, 20-inch 14-spoke polished Diamond wheel with a dark centre cap, a signature '51' badge on the front wings and an optional two-tone paint job (with one colour running over the bonnet, roof and flowing down to the boot). The vehicles (including a Continental GTC with Imperial Blue as a main and secondary hide, Linen seat and door inserts and Newmarket Tan as the accent colour) were unveiled at the [[Frankfurt Motor Show#2009|2009 Frankfurt Motor Show]],{{cite web|url=https://www.topspeed.com/cars/bentley/2010-bentley-continental-series-51/|title=2010 Bentley Continental Series 51|author=Simona|date=10 September 2009|work=Top Speed|access-date=24 January 2015}} followed by the Continental GTC model in 2010 at the [[North American International Auto Show#2010|North American International Auto Show]].{{cite web|author=Newspress Ltd |url=http://bentleymedia.com/release/245/ |title=BENTLEY MOTORS SHOWCASES NEW FLAGSHIP MULSANNE AND SERIES 51 CONTINENTAL GTC AT DETROIT MOTOR SHOW |publisher=Bentleymedia.com |date=11 January 2010 |access-date=14 June 2016}} Ordering of Series 51 models began from 1 September 2009.{{cite web|author=Newspress Ltd |url=http://bentleymedia.com/release/42/ |title=NEW SERIES 51 BENTLEY CONTINENTAL RANGE TO DEBUT AT FRANKFURT SHOW |publisher=Bentleymedia.com |access-date=14 June 2016}} ===Continental Supersports (2009–2011)=== [[File:Bentley Continental Supersports – Frontansicht (1), 18. Juli 2012, Düsseldorf.jpg|thumb|Bentley Continental Supersports coupe front view]] [[File:Bentley Continental Supersports – Heckansicht, 18. Juli 2012, Düsseldorf.jpg|thumb|Bentley Continental Supersports coupe rear view]] In February 2009, Bentley announced a limited production of the Bentley Continental Supersports. The car was unveiled at the [[Geneva Motor Show#2009|2009 Geneva Motor Show]],{{cite web|url=http://www.autoblog.com/2009/02/24/bentley-goes-green-and-really-fast-with-the-continental-sup/|title=Geneva Preview: Bentley goes green – really fast – with the Continental Supersports|author=Jonathon Ramsey|work=Autoblog|date=24 February 2009 |access-date=24 January 2015}} announced by [[Jay Leno]], to be available in autumn 2009 worldwide, followed by FlexFuel-compatible models in North America by summer 2010. The first Bentley capable of running on both [[motor spirit]] and biofuel ([[E85]] ethanol), its 6.0 litre [[W12 engine]] is rated at {{convert|630|PS|kW bhp|0|abbr=on}} at 6,000 rpm and {{convert|800|Nm|0|abbr=on}} at 1,700–5,600 rpm – using either fuel. The car can accelerate from {{convert|0|to|100|km/h|abbr=on|1}} in 3.7 seconds and {{convert|0|to|160|km/h|abbr=on|1}} in 8.9 seconds, with a top speed of {{convert|330|km/h|1|abbr=on}}. This made it the fastest and the most powerful production Bentley ever at the time of production. The Supersports was already known as the best handling Bentley. Bentley says the Supersports can deliver 1.29 g forces on a {{Convert|300|ft|m|adj=on}} skid pad, as compared to its sibling the Continental GT speed, which can perform up to 0.98 g forces on a {{Convert|300|ft|m|adj=on}} skid pad.{{cite journal|last=Rendell|first=Julian|title=Mean Greenie|journal=[[AutoWeek]]|volume=59|issue=16|page=10|publisher=[[Crain Communications, Inc.]]|location=Detroit, Michigan|date=10 August 2009|issn= 0192-9674}} It includes a revised [[ZF Friedrichshafen|ZF]] [[ZF 6HP28 transmission#6HP 26A|6HP 28A]] [[tiptronic]] [[automatic transmission|automatic]] with a "Quickshift" system that reduces [[shift time]]s by 50%, and enables double downshifts.{{Cite web|url=https://www.autoblog.com/2010/01/27/first-drive-bentley-continental-supersports-is-a-whiter/|title=First Drive: Bentley Continental Supersports is a whiter lighter shade of pale awesome|website=Autoblog|date=27 January 2010 |language=en|access-date=18 May 2019}} The car uses a [[Torsen]] T-3 centre differential for the 40:60 rear-biased torque split for the [[four-wheel drive]] system. Other changes include revised Continuous Damping Control (CDC),{{Cite web|url=https://www.topspeed.com/cars/bentley/2010-bentley-continental-supersports/|website=TopSpeed.com|access-date=18 May 2019|title=2010 Bentley Continental Supersports @ Top Speed|date=25 February 2009}} 20-inch lightweight alloy wheels (with increased {{Convert|25|mm|in|1|abbr=on}} offset on rear wheels) with 275/35 ZR20 [[Pirelli]] Ultra High Performance tyres, advanced [[Robert Bosch GmbH|Bosch]] [[electronic stability control|Electronic Stability Programme]] (ESP) with switchable Dynamic Mode, [[reinforced carbon-carbon#Similar products|Carbon fibre-reinforced Silicon Carbide]] (C/SiC) ceramic disc brakes (claimed to be the largest brakes ever fitted to a production car at the time of production),{{Cite web|url=https://jalopnik.com/the-biggest-brakes-on-a-production-car-1563490159|title=The Biggest Brakes on a Production Car|last=Orlove|first=Raphael|website=Jalopnik|date=20 April 2014 |language=en-US|access-date=18 May 2019}} {{convert|110|kg|0}} weight saving over Continental GT Speed and an automatic retractable [[spoiler (automotive)|spoiler]] (deploys at {{convert|80|km/h|0|abbr=on}}).{{Cite web|url=https://www.motor1.com/news/14979/bentley-continental-supersports-to-cost-273295/|title=Bentley Continental Supersports to Cost Supersports Convertible (2010–2011)=== [[File:2010-2011 Bentley Continental (3W) Supersports convertible (2011-11-01) 01.jpg|thumb|right|Bentley Continental Supersports convertible front view]] [[File:2010-2011 Bentley Continental (3W) Supersports convertible (2011-11-01) 02.jpg|thumb|Bentley Continental Supersports rear view]] The Continental Supersports Convertible is a convertible version of the Continental Supersports coupe. It features a revised version of the [[ZF 6HP transmission#6HP 26|ZF 6HP 26]] transmission with "Quickshift," cutting shift times by 50% and enabling double downshifts. The convertible also gets new, lightweight 20-inch alloy wheels that are {{Convert|22|lb|abbr=on}} lighter than the standard wheel. The vehicle was unveiled at the [[Geneva Motor Show#2010|2010 Geneva Motor Show]]. It includes carbon-silicon carbide brakes (420x40mm cross-drilled front and 356x28mm rear), exclusive 9Jx20-inch 14-spoke alloy wheels, choice of 3 additional exclusive body colours (Moroccan Blue (bright blue), Anthracite (grey black) and Meteor (steel blue grey)), unique insignia to exterior, unique treadplates with the text 'Celebrating 60 years of manufacturing in Crewe', choice of upgraded veneers (Dark Stained Burr Walnut or Piano Black (additional veneers available at extra cost)), drilled alloy sport foot pedals, gear lever finished in knurled chrome and hide, diamond quilted hide to seat facings, door and rear quarter panels; embroidered Bentley emblem to seat facings, indented hide headlining and a Mulliner alloy fuel filler cap.{{cite web|url=http://www.autoblog.com/2006/11/14/bentley-celebrates-60-years-at-crewe/|title=Bentley celebrates 60 years at Crewe|author=Scott Davis|work=Autoblog|date=14 November 2006 |access-date=24 January 2015}} ===Continental GTC, GTC Speed 80-11 Editions (2010)=== The 80-11 models are limited (80 units per model) versions of the Continental GTC and GTC Speed for the North American market. They are built for the North American market to commemorate Bentley's six victories at the [[24 Hours of Le Mans]]. Each car includes a unique Le Mans Edition numbered badge, Le Mans Edition clock face, embroidered Le Mans badge to each headrest, tread plates with the limited edition name, unique Le Mans Edition wheels and specific interior veneers and exterior colours. It is Bentley's vision of a GT car for 2035. The car is a fully electric 2-door coupe which can accelerate from 0-60 mph in 2.5 seconds and has a top speed of 186 mph.{{Cite web|title=Bentley EXP 100 GT concept car previews electric luxury future|url=https://www.autoblog.com/2019/07/10/bentley-exp-100-gt-electric-autonomous-concept-car-revealed/|access-date=2021-01-25|website=Autoblog|date=10 July 2019 |language=en}}{{Cite web|title=EXP 100 GT Concept|url=https://www.bentleymotors.com/en/world-of-bentley/the-bentley-story/future/exp-100-gt-concept.html|access-date=2021-01-25|website=en|language=en}} {{clear}} ==Motorsports== ===First generation (2003–2011)=== In early 2007, a Bentley Continental GT Speed equipped with Nokian Hakkapeliitta Sport Utility 5 studded winter tyres and driven by four-time World Rally Champion [[Juha Kankkunen]], broke the World Speed Record on Ice – on the frozen [[Baltic Sea]] near [[Oulu]], Finland. It averaged {{convert|321.6|km/h|2|abbr=on}} in both directions on the "flying kilometre", reaching a maximum speed of {{convert|331|km/h|2|abbr=on}}. The previous record was {{convert|296|km/h|1|abbr=on}}, achieved with a [[Bugatti EB110]] Supersport. The record-breaking Bentley was largely standard except for a roll-cage, aerodynamic improvements, low-temperature fuel and calibration.{{cite web|url=http://www.classicdriver.com/uk/magazine/3300.asp?id=13325 |title=World Speed Record on Ice for Bentley Continental GT – Classic Driver – MAGAZINE – news |publisher=Classic Driver |access-date=25 December 2009}} In February 2011, Bentley succeeded in breaking their own land-ice speed record previously set by the Continental GT. extract: The Bentley Continental GT is a grand touring car manufactured and marketed by the British company Bentley Motors since 2003. The Continental GT is offered as a two-door coupé or convertible, with four seats. It was the first new Bentley released after the company's acquisition by Volkswagen AG in 1998, and the first Bentley to employ mass production manufacturing techniques. It was later joined by the Bentley Continental Flying Spur, a four-door saloon car variant.
